messages:
Cara: Heads-up — noticed a ~2.2x p50 regression on Mixtral workloads after the kernel-selector change. Root signal points to fallback to a naive matmul for head_dim=96 which used to hit an optimized kernel.

Matt: profiling-bot uploaded trace: https://internal/pf/trace/abc123 — selector log shows flash_attn_v2 rejected due to mask shape mismatch, we fall back to triton_naive.

profiling-bot: summary: model=mixtral-8b seq=1024 batch=8 head_dim=96 -> flash_attention skipped (mask dims) -> fallback kernel increases p50 from 210ms to 460ms.

Sophie: repro snippet I used:
```
# simplified launch config
model: mixtral-8b
head_dim: 96
rope_scale: 1.0
batching: continuous
seq_len: 1024
```
Ran locally with our nightly runtime. FlashAttention call throws a mask-size check and selector chooses triton_naive.

Rahul: error excerpt from selector: 
```
W kernel_selector: flash_attn_v2 incompatible: mask_dims(seq=1024,k_dim=96) not supported -> reason: mask_strides mismatch
E kernel: fallback to triton_naive
```

Lee: additional observation: KV-cache layout assumes 64/128 alignment. For head_dim=96 we do an extra memcpy/pad when writing KV which spikes memory bandwidth and adds ~20% overhead on steady-state generation.

Cara: concrete asks: can we (A) tune selector to prefer SDPA/Triton for non-16-aligned head dims, (B) evaluate zero-padding head_dim at kernel-launch as short-term mitigation, and (C) update batching heuristics to split batches by head_dim bucket so we don't mix incompatible models in the same dynamic batch?

Sophie: tried padding approach: zero-pad KV to next multiple of 8 at kernel entry. Quick numbers: p50 down ~8% vs triton_naive fallback, memory +3% and small extra memcpy cost but still better than naive. Quality unaffected in our eval prompts. Code: 
```
// pad k_dim to 104 (next multiple of 8) and launch flash_attn with padded tensors
```

Matt: note: flashattn_v2 sometimes expects head_dim%16==0 for certain vectorized fused kernels; SDPA handles %8 but has a mask edge-case when rope_scale != 1.0 and using fp16 (we saw tiny numerical diffs).

Rahul: plan from infra: I can land selector change to prefer sdpa/triton for head_dim%16!=0 + add a runtime flag to force-pad heads. Will open PR and add unit tests for mask shape detection. Owning short-term.

Lee: medium-term we should fix mask handling inside flash_attn_v2 so it can accept arbitrary head dims (or at least %8) without triggering stride/mask mismatch. That will remove need for padding and reduce mem overhead. Also add KV-cache alignment metadata to traces so we can correlate mem copies with latency spikes.

profiling-bot: quick A/B after Rahul's selector tweak on canary: mixtral-8b/seq1024 batch8 -> p50: 210ms -> 145ms (10% traffic). End-to-end cost drops ~28% on that slice.

Sophie: one gotcha — RoPE scaling >1.0 changes attention magnitude and exposes fp16 accumulation instabilities in SDPA in a few prompts. Short-term we should clip attention logits before softmax for SDPA when rope_scale != 1.0. Adding to TODO.

Cara: Action items summarized: 
- Rahul: PR to prefer sdpa/triton for head_dim%16!=0 + runtime force-pad flag (short-term).
- Sophie: measure pad tradeoffs across mixtral/qwen/llama variants, push eval results to regression board.
- Lee: instrument KV-cache alignment in traces, measure memcpy hotspots.
- Matt: own canary rollout plan for Dedicated pool (10% A, 90% control) and rollback hooks.
- Engineering: spec change to batching heuristic: group by (seq_len, head_dim_bucket, rope_scale_bucket).

Sophie: I've pushed an eval set to the regression board: https://evals/board/xyz — includes long-context samples and rope_scale=1.2 tests.

Matt: SGTM. Can we sync tomorrow 10:00AM eng-runtime to triage PRs and canary windows?

Cara: yep — thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
